title: etask schema v2
description: Grammar for etask code-generation schemas: a tree of scopes, abstract scopes and tasks.

identifier.description: A valid C++ identifier (becomes a namespace/class/directory).

params.description: Ordered name -> type map. Declaration order is the wire contract.

statusKey.description: A status_code a completing task can send: the task/runtime range (finished and aborted alias task_finished/task_aborted), or custom(0xNN) in 0x70-0xFF. Manager/API codes - including ok - and the framework-owned result_too_large cannot key a shape.

resultShape.description: One result shape: named map or positional list of types (ordered - order is the wire contract).

oneOf.description: One shape per status code. The reply's status byte is what tells a peer which shape it received.

returns.description: Either one result shape (carried by an ordinary completion, i.e. task_finished), or a mapping of status code -> shape. The two forms are told apart by the values: type strings mean a single shape, nested shapes mean status-keyed. Mixing them is an error.

type.description: Which tier this task is, and so which lifecycle hooks it carries and what it costs. instant_task: fire-and-forget, runs on arrival inside the delivering call, no reply, no storage, no vtable. oneshot_task: runs once and replies. polled_task: runs across ticks and decides when it is done. stateful_task: a polled task that can be paused and resumed.

concurrency.description: How many instances of this task's uid may run concurrently (default 1). Lowered to capacity<T, N> in the generated task_list. Not valid on an instant_task, which occupies no storage.

then.description: An instant_task has no on_complete and sends no reply, so it can declare neither a result shape nor a concurrency limit.
